Confusable pairs among the insurance and crash rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, the bureau's mailing address and fax number are agency contact details and are not taught, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
Bodily injury minimums differ by scope: $25,000 for one person but $50,000 for all injuries in one crash. [A01]
Why it matters: group coverage; confusable per person versus per crash; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
Property damage coverage has a single minimum of $25,000 per crash, the same figure as the per person bodily injury minimum. [A01]
Why it matters: group coverage; confusable property damage versus bodily injury; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A01
Uninsured motorist coverage uses the same $25,000 and $50,000 bodily injury amounts, and the guide lists no property damage amount for it. [A01]
Why it matters: group coverage; confusable uninsured motorist versus liability; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A01
A regular surety bond, certificate of deposit or security is filed at $75,000, while a real estate bond must be $150,000. [A01]
Why it matters: group financial responsibility; confusable bond amounts; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A01
Self-insurance needs more than 25 vehicles, so an owner with exactly 25 vehicles does not qualify. [A01]
Why it matters: group financial responsibility; threshold edge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A01
Most drivers get liability insurance from an insurance company or agent rather than through self-insurance, bonds or cash. [A01]
Why it matters: group financial responsibility; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A02
The insurance suspension fees climb from $20 for one suspension to $200 for two and $400 for three or more. [A02]
Why it matters: group suspensions; confusable fee ladder; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A02
Two suspensions count as a repeat only when they fall within two years of each other, but proof of insurance must then be kept for three years. [A02]
Why it matters: group suspensions; confusable two years versus three years; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A02
An unpaid-damages suspension and a third insurance suspension both last one year, but early reinstatement from the first costs $20 while the second carries a $400 fee. [A02]
Why it matters: group suspensions; confusable one-year suspensions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A03
After a minor crash with no injuries you move the vehicle off the road, but you never move an injured person. [A03]
Why it matters: group crash steps; confusable vehicle versus person; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A03
The Move It law's campaign phrase is steer it and clear it, and signs with that message are being posted in the St. Louis and Kansas City areas. [A03]
Why it matters: group Move It law; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A03
The Missouri Department of Transportation used the law's tenth anniversary to remind drivers to clear minor crashes from the road. [A03]
Why it matters: group Move It law; dynamic campaign timing.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A03
Driving responsibly and defensively lowers the chance of a crash, but nothing can prevent crashes entirely. [A03]
Why it matters: group crashes; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A04
The damage threshold for a required report is property damage greater than $500, so damage of exactly $500 without injury does not meet it. [A04]
Why it matters: group accident report; threshold edge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A04
Even when a report is not required, you may still file one if an uninsured motorist was involved, though the Department can act only against that motorist for not keeping insurance. [A04]
Why it matters: group accident report; continuation of optional reports.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A04
The uninsured-party condition and the damage-or-injury condition are joined by the word and, so both must be true before a report is required. [A04]
Why it matters: group accident report; confusable all versus any condition; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]
